title: Linear Search
summary: Scan left to right and return the first index whose value equals the target.
usage:
How it works
No sorting is required. After checking index i without a match, all earlier indices are known not to contain the target. Useful for small or unsorted collections, and when you need the first occurrence. Returns a zero-based index or -1 if absent; an empty input returns -1.

Properties and prerequisites
Precondition: none beyond a valid array. Does not modify input. Duplicates: returns first occurrence.

Complexity
Time: O(n) worst/average; O(1) best. Space: O(1).

Example
Input: [5, 2, 4, 1, 3]; target = 1. Output: index 3.

Try it
Use Play/Pause, Previous/Next, the timeline, and playback speed. Answer the prediction checkpoints to continue; feedback reveals the expected answer.
